I would like to propose The Age of Reverence, an age where gods will require the support of at-least two other gods in order to take any action that has the goal of influencing or effecting (both positively and negatively) any of the mortal races on Gaea. If a race decides to pray to a god, asking for help and the like, that god may act to influence or effect that race (whether they want to play nice or not is up to them) without aforementioned restriction

Edit: Once a race has made a post about praying to a god, that race must make another post about halting their prayers before a god once again becomes limited in his actions toward that race.

I don't like that any race can ask for and get unlimited divine intervention. Which brings back the divine spam from the last war.

I also don't like the idea of "goals" since that's impossible to tell even if it was well defined. If Phyra for example wants to create more order and performs actions in service of that goal than the goal isn't effecting a mortal race, even if the action is to kill everything. And that's assuming gods are honest about their goals.

Get rid of those loopholes and we basically have my suggestion.

As with all things, actions can still be voted on. This simply provides a barrier between the races and the gods, a barrier that is controlled by the races themselves. I'll also be leaving it to the community to decide if any particular action appears to have the goal of influencing or effecting a race without meeting the prerequisites of having the support of two other gods or having the race pray to them..

I actually think giving people control over the barrier is far worse than not having the barrier at all, since now it can be manipulated for one-sided intervention.

On the other side, how many actions affect only one race? It could be argued that every action affects all races to some extent so all races will have to ask for that god's intervention before it can happen.

Actions will indeed effect multiple races, but that goes back to the goal or the intent of the action. If I were to bless the deva with the knowledge needed to construct laser weapons, other races may well learn from the deva how to make and use these weapons. However, my actions and intent primarily targeted the deva, therefore only the deva would need to pray to me for me to get this action allowed without the assistance of other gods.

And how is intent determined? Does it have to be explicitly stated? What if an intent doesn't mention any races?

And what if a race asks you to smite its enemies?

There are far too many holes in this, far more than the "direct action" heuristic we argued about before.

If the intent of an action is unclear, you are free to ask for clarification and get an arbiter involved.

If a race asks you to smite their enemies, you still need the aid of two other gods in order to follow up that request unless the race they ask you to smite is a race that is currently worshiping you
